_comment: Hand-maintained venue list. `tracked` venues have a scraper in scrapers/<scraper>.js; `more` venues are link-only. The site and the scraper both read this file.

tracked.name: AFI Silver Theatre
tracked.blurb: Three screens of repertory series, restorations, 35mm prints and new arthouse releases.

tracked.name: Avalon Theatre
tracked.blurb: Nonprofit neighborhood movie house, open since 1923. New independent releases plus international series.

tracked.name: Suns Cinema
tracked.blurb: Single-screen bar and cinema programming cult, classic and international films. 21+.

tracked.name: Angelika Pop-Up at Union Market
tracked.blurb: Three small screens: new independent and international releases, plus weekly classics series.

tracked.name: 4EYE Film Center
tracked.blurb: Nonprofit arthouse cinema that opened in October 2026 at the Revada Arts Center. Independent, classic and international film.

tracked.name: Miracle Theatre
tracked.blurb: Historic single-screen house on Capitol Hill. Mostly live shows these days, with second-run and classic films in between.

tracked.name: National Gallery of Art
tracked.address: East Building, 4th St & Constitution Ave NW
tracked.blurb: Free weekend film series in the East Building auditorium: retrospectives, restorations and artists' film.

tracked.name: Library of Congress
tracked.blurb: Occasional free screenings drawn from the national film collection.

more.name: Landmark Atlantic Plumbing Cinema
more.why: Landmark's remaining DC theater. New independent and studio releases.

more.name: Alamo Drafthouse DC
more.why: Chain multiplex with regular repertory and cult programming.

more.name: Edlavitch DCJCC / JxJ
more.why: Film programs and the annual JxJ festival.

more.name: Greenbelt Cinema
more.why: Nonprofit art deco movie house (the Old Greenbelt Theatre). New independent releases and classics.

more.name: Arlington Cinema & Drafthouse
more.why: Movies with food and drink, between comedy shows.
